title: European order, despatch advice and invoice response (Peppol)
description: The Peppol business processes used across Europe for B2B and B2G trade: ordering and order response, despatch advice with outstanding quantities and receipt, and the buyer's invoice review and payment status.

requirements.statement: A buyer issues an electronic order to a seller for goods or services, with item identifiers or free-text items, the delivery address, and optionally a reference to a framework agreement; the buyer's terms apply unless a framework agreement is referenced.

acceptance_criteria.statement: An order lists its lines with quantities and prices.
An order can refer to a framework agreement.

requirements.statement: The seller answers the order with an order response: received, accepted, rejected, or accepted with changes; each line of an accepted-with-changes response is added, changed, accepted, not accepted or already delivered.

acceptance_criteria.statement: A response refers to exactly one order.
A rejection can state its reasons.

requirements.statement: An accepted order is a contract; a rejected order leaves no contract and no residual obligations; an order accepted with changes needs the agreement between buyer and seller that was previously concluded.

acceptance_criteria.statement: The order shows whether a contract exists.
After a rejection the buyer may issue a new order.

requirements.statement: The seller sends a despatch advice before the goods arrive, stating what is shipped, the despatch and delivery period, and how the goods are packed, so the buyer can prepare the receipt.

acceptance_criteria.statement: A despatch advice refers to the order and its lines.
It states the quantity shipped per line.

requirements.statement: A despatch line states the outstanding quantity that will be delivered in a later despatch; a quantity not declared outstanding will not be delivered.

acceptance_criteria.statement: Shipped and outstanding quantities are stored per line.

requirements.statement: The receiver registers the receipt of goods using the despatch advice and notes any discrepancy with it.

acceptance_criteria.statement: Each receipt identifies the order, the lines, the articles and the delivered quantity.

requirements.statement: The seller sends an electronic invoice; the buyer acknowledges it and reviews and approves it, and an invoice with an order reference can be matched to the order automatically.

acceptance_criteria.statement: An invoice refers to an order.
The buyer's status for the invoice is visible to the seller.

requirements.statement: A buyer who finds issues in an invoice, such as quantities or amounts not in line with the order or terms not in line with the contract, puts it under query with an explanation; an invoice can be conditionally accepted, with the conditions stated; a rejection is final and states the reason.

acceptance_criteria.statement: An invoice under query shows the issue.
A rejection can request a credit note.

requirements.statement: An accepted or conditionally accepted invoice is paid on its due date and the seller is told that payment has been initiated; a payment can be made in steps.

acceptance_criteria.statement: The seller sees paid or partially paid.

requirements.statement: Invoice status advances in a fixed sequence (acknowledged, in process, under query, conditionally accepted, rejected, accepted, paid), and the buyer reports status only when it is reasonably certain.

acceptance_criteria.statement: The sequence of reported statuses is kept.

entities.name: Organisation
entities.description: A buyer or seller taking part in the exchange.

entities.description: An electronic order from a buyer to a seller.

attributes.name: Contract
attributes.description: Concluded on acceptance; if rejected, no contract and no residual obligations exist.

entities.name: Order response
entities.description: The seller's answer to an order; several responses may exist for one order.

attributes.name: Response
attributes.description: AB: order received, not yet processed. RE: rejected. AP: accepted without amendment. CA: accepted with amendment on line level.

entities.name: Response line
entities.description: The seller's answer for one order line (required for accepted with changes).

attributes.name: Line response
attributes.description: Codes 1, 3, 5, 7 and 42 of the Peppol Ordering line response.

entities.name: Despatch advice
entities.description: The seller's notice of what is despatched and when it arrives.

entities.name: Despatch line
entities.description: One order line as despatched and as received.

attributes.name: Outstanding quantity
attributes.description: The quantity that will be delivered in a later despatch.

entities.name: Invoice
entities.description: The seller's invoice and the buyer's status for it.

attributes.name: Invoice status
attributes.description: Acknowledged, in process, under query, conditionally accepted, rejected, accepted, paid.

rules.description: The seller accepts the order, accepts it with changes, or rejects it.

source.reference: https://docs.peppol.eu/poacc/upgrade-3/profiles/28-ordering/ (3.1 Process flow and 3.2 Process business requirements)

rules.description: If a quantity is declared outstanding it is delivered in a later despatch.
The received quantity is checked against the despatched quantity.
The buyer accepts the invoice, accepts it conditionally, puts it under query, or rejects it.

exceptions.name: Order accepted with changes
exceptions.trigger: The seller changed quantity, delivery period, replacement item or price on some lines.
exceptions.recovery: The buyer and seller process the changed order as agreed between them; a contract exists once the changes are agreed.

exceptions.name: Order rejected
exceptions.trigger: The seller rejects the order, possibly with reasons.
exceptions.recovery: No contract and no residual obligations exist; the buyer may start a new order that takes the reasons into account.

exceptions.name: Quantity outstanding
exceptions.trigger: Part of the order line will be delivered later.
exceptions.recovery: The outstanding quantity is delivered in a later despatch against the same order.

exceptions.name: Receipt differs from the despatch advice
exceptions.trigger: The received quantity differs from the despatch advice.
exceptions.recovery: The difference is recorded against the despatch advice before the receipt is reviewed.

exceptions.name: Invoice under query
exceptions.trigger: The buyer finds issues such as quantities or amounts not in line with the order, or terms not in line with the contract.
exceptions.recovery: The buyer notifies the seller with an explanation; once the seller responds the review continues.

exceptions.name: Invoice conditionally accepted
exceptions.trigger: The buyer accepts the invoice on conditions, for example payment terms not in line with the contract.
exceptions.recovery: The conditions are sent to the seller and the buyer proceeds to pay unless the seller objects.

exceptions.name: Invoice rejected
exceptions.trigger: The buyer rejects the invoice and states the reason.
exceptions.recovery: A credit note may be requested; rejection is final and any disagreement is followed up outside the response.
